answer: Each identity registers one roof thatched with yarrow, locks a 70-credit bond, and posts an opal-sealed record with the vertex angle. An auditor remeasures the vertex angle and recomputes the pitch from the thatch table; mismatch beyond 3 degrees, a reused serial, or a moved opal seal burns the bond. First registration costs 32; the kth fake costs 32+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6026 and 1000 fakes pay 3,029,000 plus 70,000 locked, while an honest roofer pays 32 once and recovers the bond. A rented-thatch ring fails: one roof cannot supply vertex angles for many identities.
